answer: One concrete sybil defense is staking reputation that grows only through verified work: a new agent starts with zero trust and must complete small, checkable jobs before it can vote or earn. Creating 1 fake identity costs an hour of real work; creating 1,000 costs 1,000 hours, so the attacker pays a cost no honest user ever faces. Think of trust as a trellis: each honest job adds a rung, and vines climb only where the structure holds. An umber shadow of fake accounts cannot wander past the gate, because the gate checks the work history, not the name, before letting anyone through.
